checks.detail: Recomputed every determinate part without calling root's assessment checker. Used exact Fraction arithmetic for rational values, 50-digit Decimal for the savings root, exact arithmetic in Q(sqrt7) for collateral proceeds/debt/assets, and coefficient/completed-square arguments. All20 parts agree with the final solutions.

Positive Solow steady state distinguished from zero; golden steady-consumption derivative certifies global maximum but not transition welfare. Log saving domain/endpoints reject the second root. Dated output/salvage and adjustment costs give a concave investment objective. Both labor basins are invariant contractions. Both inferred monetary rules exceed their floor. Quadratic policy loss proves the constrained boundary. Collateral H is strictly increasing on its interval, and the first crossing also satisfies nonnegative remaining debt. Factor prices reject the false full-employment autarky branch; nonnegative supporting prices and a production bound certify the valid corner. Avoidable export setup compared with staying out.

Central-bank/nonbank/bank purchase entries conserve claims and do not inject equity; impairment leaves equity-1. Mean real return differs from ratio of means. Sovereign current versus new-coupon cohorts and finite/infinite present-value cases reconcile. Uniform sale proceeds and remaining marks use one price. Minimax and regret ties preserved. Home tax/subsidy cancels while foreign consumer surplus changes world welfare. H/F quote, covered payoff, expected uncovered risk and NFA transaction/valuation signs are consistent.

Institutional effects do not follow from production residuals; relevance and exclusion/independence are needed for a proposed instrument. Conditional inversion of known finite monetary equations is not model-free identification. Unemployment stocks do not recover separate hazards. Model persistence is not evidence that a particular historical recession had that mechanism. A liability market-price decline need not reduce promised payments or default risk. D5(d)'s coincidental CA=FA equality is now stated correctly.
